china_race_dynamics.text: China wants to beat us in artificial intelligence. I don't want China to lead in that. I want the country that has the First Amendment, respects religious freedom, the freedom of the press, and freedom of speech. That's the country that I want to lead in data centers and in AI. And that's the United States. So we have to lead.

deepseek.reason: The speaker says China wants to beat the US in AI and that the US must lead, making competition with China a priority.
deepseek.confidence_reason: Explicitly frames AI leadership as a contest with China and calls for the US to lead.

china_race_dynamics.text: I welcome discussions and debate on the federal level about our nation's infrastructure needs to power innovation and maintain a competitive edge over rivals such as Communist China, but that should not come at the expense of higher utility bills for Colorado families,

deepseek.reason: The speaker welcomes federal discussion of infrastructure to maintain a competitive edge over China, conditioned on avoiding higher utility bills.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The statement endorses maintaining a competitive edge over China, though with a cost condition.

china_race_dynamics.text:
Permitting delays are holding America back. To unleash American energy, meet rising demand, and beat China in the AI race, we need a permitting system that works. 

That’s why I supported the SPEED Act in @NatResources markup - and will support it on the floor tomorrow.

deepseek.reason: The speaker says permitting reform is needed to beat China in the AI race and supports the SPEED Act.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The statement explicitly frames beating China in the AI race as a reason for the policy he supports.
